text:
Maya: Heads-up — seeing weird KV cache occupancy skew on the canary for gpt-mini-v3. Shard 3 is at ~92% while others are 10–25%. Eviction rate spikes correlate with 95p decode latency up ~30ms. Anyone seen this?
Sam: Ugh. Do you have the prom query and a short log sample?
Maya: Prom query I used (range):
```
curl -s 'https://prom.redwood/api/v1/query_range?query=kvcache_occupancy_percent%7Bmodel%3D%22gpt-mini-v3%22%7D&start=1769997600&end=1769997760&step=15'
```
Maya: And a short tail from the evict logs on that host: 
```
[2026-03-12T14:02:13Z] shard=3 evict_start count=120 ttl=0 hit_rate=0.021
[2026-03-12T14:02:14Z] shard=3 evict_item id=0x7fb21a ... size=512
[2026-03-12T14:02:15Z] shard=3 evict_done freed=48ms
[2026-03-12T14:02:20Z] shard=1 evict_start count=3
```
Maya: Noticed eviction work only in shard=3, others nearly idle.
Zach: :eyes: Could be skewed key distribution or a buggy shard hash. Have you run kv_dump for hot keys on that instance?
Maya: Not yet. Wanted to check before running heavy tools. Can we run a quick probe that samples key prefixes for shard 3?
Sam: You can use `kv_dump --shard 3 --sample 1000 --out /tmp/shard3-sample.json`. It'll be noisy but fast.
Anya: I can run that on the canary now. Which binary version and config? Might be important — we had a change in kv routing last week.
Maya: Canary is `runtime@v2.13.1+hotfix` and config `kv.partition=mod_hash` (default). Sample command I ran earlier for occupancy: `./tools/kv-stats --json --shard=3 --window=60`. Output showed a small set of prefixes accounting for ~78% of live entries.
Zach: If a few prefixes dominate, it's probably prefix skew not eviction bug. We should also check `kv_prefix_hash(prefix)` distribution. Can you paste sample prefixes (redact content) or counts?
Maya: Pasted counts (redacted) — `{"p0":54000, "p1":4700, "p2":3200, "others":1200}`. p0 looks crazy.
InfraBot: [alert] High KV eviction rate on host canary-03 (shard=3) at 2026-03-12T14:02:00Z, tag=eviction-spike.
Liam: Two quick hypotheses: 1) upstream traffic has a routing change causing many requests with same prefix, 2) a recent feature started caching long-lived keys under same prefix. Also consider sample bias if sampling logic uses modulo on key hash.
Sam: Agreed. Maya, can you run `kv_dump --top-prefixes 20` and also export `kvcache_latency{shard,operation}` for last 10m?
Maya: Running `kv_dump` now; ETA ~2m. Prom query for latency I ran: 
```
avg_over_time(kvcache_latency_seconds_sum{shard="3"}/kvcache_latency_seconds_count{shard="3"}[10m])
```
Anya: While that's running I can also start a short synthetic load that mimics prod routing to confirm whether the skew reproduces under controlled load. Which seed and prompt set?
Maya: Use seed=42 and the `inference-sample-v1` prompt set. Also use client headers X-Route: ab-test-02 to mimic real traffic.
Zach: If `p0` is dominated by a partially normalized user id, maybe upstream normalization changed. Add a quick histogram of prefix lengths: `kvcache_prefix_length_bucket` — that might show if one prefix is very long/unique.
Maya: kv_dump output (top prefixes):
```
{"prefix":"usr:acct:12345","count":54000}
{"prefix":"sys:temp","count":4700}
{"prefix":"sess:abcd","count":3200}
...rest...
```
Maya: The `usr:acct:12345` pattern is suspicious — a single account ID.
Anya: Running synthetic load now against canary-03 with X-Route header. Will watch shard occupancy and eviction.
Sam: If it's a single account, we can consider bloom-prefetch or per-prefix TTL to avoid never-ending residency. But first we need to know access pattern: frequent short-lived keys or one large keyset?
Maya: Access pattern shows repeated reads and some writes; mostly reads during the window. Eviction churn suggests write churn too though.
Liam: Quick mitigation: temporarily increase `kv.shard[3].high_watermark` by 10% on canary and monitor latencies. That buys time for deeper analysis. But coordinate with SRE for memory.
Anya: Synthetic run results: after 3m, shard=3 occupancy moved from 92% -> 95% and eviction rate stayed high. So load reproduces.
Zach: Confirms hotspot. Next steps: 1) instrument `kv_prefix_access_count` per-prefix (low-overhead histogram) for short window, 2) dump key hashes for p0 to see sub-prefix entropy, 3) consider redirecting that account's traffic to a separate cache class (hot partition) or apply per-prefix eviction TTL.
Maya: I'll open an ops ticket with the p0 owner (account team) and ask for clarification on traffic. Can someone prepare a small PR to add `kv_prefix_access_count` metric and a debug endpoint to output top prefixes without full dump?
Sam: I'll sketch a PR today. Ping me with repo and I can add tests.
Liam: I'll coordinate increasing high_watermark on canary-03 for 1 hour now. If infra sees memory issues, I'll rollback.
Anya: I'll follow up with full kv_dump and upload artifacts to the thread.
Maya: Thanks all. Summary/todo: 
- Anya: full kv_dump + synthetic results (action)
- Sam: PR to add per-prefix access metric and a non-blocking top-prefix endpoint (action)
- Liam: temporary high_watermark bump on canary-03 (action)
- Maya: open ops ticket + contact account owner (action)
- Zach: help review PR and look at hash distribution code (action)
Maya: tagging next check-in in ~2 hours :clock2: :thumbsup:
